butir.teks: Explanation of the Variation Among Selves in Intellect

People have differed over the variation in intellect, and there is no point in busying ourselves with relating the words of those whose attainment is slight; rather, what is better and more important is to hasten to state the truth plainly.

The plain truth on this is to say that variation extends to the four categories except the second, which is the necessary knowledge of the possibility of the possible and the impossibility of the impossible.

For whoever knows that two is more than one also knows the impossibility of a body being in two places, and of one thing being both eternal and originated, and likewise all similar cases, and everything he perceives with verified perception free of doubt. As for the other three categories, variation does extend to them. As for the fourth category, which is the power's gaining mastery over the suppression of appetites, the variation among people in it is not hidden; indeed the variation in the states of a single person in it is not hidden. This variation is at times due to variation in the appetite, since an intelligent person may be able to give up some appetites but not others; but it is not confined to that.

For a young man may be unable to give up fornication, and when he grows older and his intellect is complete, he is able to. The appetite for showing off (riya') and for leadership grows stronger with age, not weaker. At times its cause is the variation in the knowledge that makes known the danger of that appetite. For this reason the physician is able to guard against certain harmful foods, and he has precedence in that over one equal to him in intellect

if he is not a physician, even though he believes in a general way that there is harm in it; but when the physician's knowledge is more complete, his fear is stronger, so fear becomes an army for the intellect and a provision for it in suppressing the appetites and breaking them.

Likewise the scholar is more able than the ignorant person to give up acts of disobedience because of the strength of his knowledge of the harm of disobedience. By the scholar I mean the true scholar, not the possessors of scholarly shawls and the people of raving.

If the variation comes from the side of appetite, it does not go back to variation in intellect; but if it comes from the side of knowledge, then we have named this kind of knowledge intellect as well, for it strengthens the innate disposition of the intellect, so the variation lies in that to which the naming refers. And at times it is due merely to variation in the innate disposition of the intellect, for when that is strong, its suppression of appetite is inevitably more intense.

As for the third category, which is the knowledge of experience, the variation of people in it cannot be denied, for they differ in frequency of hitting upon what is right and in speed of perception. Its cause is either a variation in the innate disposition or a variation in practice. As for the first, which is the basis, I mean the innate disposition, there is no way to reject the variation in it, for it is like a light that shines upon the self; its dawn rises and the beginnings of its shining appear at the age of discernment. Then it keeps growing, increasing with a growth whose gradual stages are unnoticeable, until it is complete near the age of forty. Its likeness is the light of dawn: its first beginnings are hidden, so subtly that it is hard to perceive, then it progresses in increase until it is complete with the rising of the disc of the sun.

The variation in the light of insight is like the variation in the light of sight, and the difference is perceptible between the weak-eyed and the keen-sighted. Rather, the way (sunna) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, runs through all His creation by gradual stages in bringing into being, so that the innate disposition of appetite does not appear in the boy at puberty all at once and suddenly, but appears little by little, gradually; and so it is with all the faculties and attributes. Whoever denies the variation among people in this innate disposition is as though cast off from the bond of intellect, and whoever thinks that the intellect of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) is like the intellect of ordinary peasants and the coarse people of the desert is baser in himself than ordinary peasants. How can the variation in innate disposition be denied, when without it people would not differ in understanding the sciences, nor be divided into the dull-witted, who does not understand even when made to understand except after long toil from the teacher, the intelligent, who understands from the slightest hint and sign, and the perfect, from whose own self the realities of things well up without teaching, as Allah Most High says, ⟦QS 24:35⟧ Such is the case of the prophets (peace be upon them), for obscure matters become clear to them within their inner selves without learning or hearing, and this is expressed as inspiration (ilham). Of the like of this the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) spoke when he said, "The Holy Spirit blew into my heart: love whom you will, for you will part from him; live as long as you will, for you will die; and do what you will, for you will be repaid for it." (١) This kind of the angels' making known to the prophets differs from explicit revelation (wahy), which is hearing a voice with the sense of the ear and seeing the angel with the sense of sight; for this reason he reported this one as a blowing into the heart. The degrees of revelation are many, and delving into them is not fitting for the knowledge of conduct ('ilm al-mu'amala); it belongs to the knowledge of unveiling ('ilm al-mukashafa).

Do not suppose that knowing the degrees of revelation requires the rank of revelation, for it is not far-fetched that a sick physician knows the degrees of health, and that a sinful scholar knows the degrees of justice though he is devoid of it. Knowledge is one thing and the existence of the thing known is another. Not everyone who knows prophethood and the friendship of Allah (walaya) is a prophet or a friend of Allah (wali), nor is everyone who knows God-consciousness (taqwa) and scrupulousness (wara') and their subtleties God-conscious.

The division of people into those who become alert of themselves and understand, those who understand only with alerting and teaching, and those whom neither teaching nor alerting benefits, is like the division of the earth into land in which water gathers and grows strong and gushes forth of itself as springs, land that needs digging so that the water may be brought out into channels, and land in which digging is of no benefit, namely the dry. That is due to the difference in the substances of the earth in their attributes; so likewise is the difference of selves in the innate disposition of intellect.

Evidence for the variation in intellect from the side of transmission is what is related, that 'Abd Allah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him) asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in a long hadith, at the end of which is a description of the greatness of the Throne, and that the angels said, "Our Lord, have You created anything greater than the Throne?"

He said, "Yes, the intellect." They said, "And how great is its measure?" He said, "Far from it! Its measure cannot be encompassed by knowledge. Do you have knowledge of the number of the sand?" They said, "No." Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said, "I have created the intellect in various kinds, like the number of the sand. Among people are those who are given one grain, and among them those given two grains, and among them those given three and four, and among them those given a faraq, and among them those given a wasq, and among them those given more than that." (١)

If you say, "Then what is the matter with groups of the Sufis who condemn the intellect as the rational (ma'qul)?", know that the reason is that people transferred the name of the intellect, the rational, to disputation and debate by means of contradictions and imposed conclusions, which is the craft of theology (kalam). The Sufis were unable to establish with them that "You have erred in the naming," since it could not be effaced from their hearts after tongues had passed it around and it had taken root in the hearts; so they condemned the intellect and the rational, which is what bears that name among them.

As for the light of insight by which Allah Most High is known and the truthfulness of His messengers is known, how can its condemnation be conceived, when Allah Most High has praised it? And if it is condemned, what is there after it that is praised? If what is praised is the revealed law (shar'), by what was the soundness of the revealed law known? If it was known by the condemned intellect, which cannot be trusted, then the revealed law too would be condemned. No attention is paid to one who says that it is perceived by the eye of certainty and the light of faith, not by the intellect, for by the intellect we mean what he means by the eye of certainty and the light of faith, namely the inner attribute by which the human being is distinguished from the beasts, so that he perceives by it the realities of things. Most of these confusions arose only from the ignorance of people who sought realities from words and so floundered in them because of the confusion of people's conventions about words. This much suffices in explaining the intellect, and Allah knows best.

The Book of Knowledge is complete, with the praise of Allah Most High and by His favour; and may Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad and upon every chosen servant among the inhabitants of the earth and the heaven.
